messages.text:
Hi Luis,

Odd day to send this, I know, but the studio is quiet and I'm finally getting to the list I made in November.

I'm Odile, I look after partnerships at Moth & Lantern. We're a nine-person motion and illustration studio in Bristol, and most of our work is for product teams who need their interfaces to move well but don't have a motion designer of their own: onboarding sequences, empty states, small loading moments, the explainer that sits on a pricing page. We work mostly as a quiet second team, under the agency's name, and the client never needs to know we exist.

For overflow it's £650 a day, or £3,500 a month for six days. We'd work in your files and hand over Lottie and video exports. The little jobs usually take about three working days.

I found Acme through the Brightwell Trust report. The year's figures on that fold-out spread caught my eye. I'd be curious to see what your team would do with the same material on screen.

If you have a screen that's been sitting in the 'animate later' pile, send it over and we'll try a free pass on it.

No need to reply now, and certainly not today. If it's useful in the new year, I'll be around from the 6th.

Happy new year when it comes.

All the best,
Odile Fairbairn
Partnerships, Moth & Lantern
Motion and illustration for product teams
Unit 4, Paintworks, Bristol BS4 3EH | mothandlantern.example

Luis -

Ran the v2 dark set against every client palette we have on file. Three fail.

Brightwell: their orange on our dark surface is 2.9:1. Links in body text are unreadable.
Tandem City: the teal is fine as a fill, but text set in it drops to 3.4:1 in dark.
Orchard Lane Housing: their purple more or less disappears on `surface.raised`. 2.1:1.

Luis Cordero

3rd floor, 48 Turnmill Street, London EC1M 5RR

facts: about to start the final year of a graphic communication degree at Kenmore School of Art in Leeds

messages.text:
Dear Luis,

Sorry for writing out of the blue. My tutor, Moira Duff, showed us Acme's work in a lecture on design for museums, and your name was on the Holloway project page, so I thought I'd try.

I'm going into the final year of a graphic communication degree at Kenmore School of Art in Leeds. Most of my work so far is print: posters, a book, a type specimen for a project with a local letterpress studio. Over the last year I've got much more interested in product and interface design, and I'd like to apply for junior product design roles next summer. My problem is that my portfolio doesn't look like a product designer's at all.

Would you put the print work in if it was the best thing you'd made? I've only got one app project I'm proud of. There's another one I did over a weekend that I could use to pad it out, but I don't really want to have to talk about it in an interview. Would two case studies be enough? I keep seeing people say eight, which seems like a lot.

Also, when you're looking through juniors' work, what actually makes you stop and read a case study? I spent Sunday changing all the type on the site again, which feels like an excellent way of avoiding the portfolio itself.

It's at rubyadair.example if you do fancy a look. Even a line back would help.

Sorry this is so long.

Thank you so much,
Ruby Adair
